correctness.rationale: All quantifiers concern proper spherical caps −1<h<1 and real axial angular frequencies. Transverse-ball integration yields the one-dimensional polynomial Fourier integral. Exact integration by parts yields the endpoint representation; three exact factorizations were symbolically verified. Strict positive endpoint-modulus difference for m=1,2 rules out nonzero real zeros; at t=0 the integral is positive. For m=3 a continuous large-frequency equal-modulus branch exists for h near −1; its endpoint ratio tends to exp(iπ/3), giving continuous unbounded phase mismatch and exact zeros at each sufficiently large integer phase winding. Asymptotics follow by expansion and finite-zero claim by uniform integration-by-parts tail for fixed height plus analyticity. Independent high-precision quadrature and 3 witness computations replayed, but finite checks are not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: Axial Fourier zeros are a natural directional null invariant of convex caps, relevant to diffraction and Fourier-null geometry. The theorem identifies sharp low-dimension rigidity (dimensions 3 and 5) broken already in dimension 7 for a sequence of proper caps arbitrarily close to the ball; the leading height-frequency asymptotics reveal a substantive endpoint-phase resonance. This is a complete low-dimension dichotomy regarding all proper h for d3,d5 and existence for d7, not a numerical curiosity. The precise parameters are naturally selected by ball cross sections and the first nontrivial breakdown, rather than an arbitrary slice.
